body:
A human can change a design directly on the page as well as through the design agent: first by editing what exists, then by dragging components around. It works on both tabs. Depends on the tabs (feature:b993a7a21b436618, feature:7c9cdfad16609a44), and on selecting an element (feature:afd9fe8bae36c59c). The process is expected to be iterative.

## Asked for

- A core requirement: users can drag and drop, and can also directly edit what exists, such as dragging a border or changing a color.
- Eventually both tabs support drag-and-drop components and WYSIWYG editing.
- A local history with undo may suit designers better than git.

## From the other agent's plan (direction, not gospel)

- Clicking an element selects it by ID, and an inspector panel shows its properties.
- Dragging an edge resizes the element, and a color picker sets colors.
- One set of operations is used by the editor, by agents, and by undo and redo.
- Later: drag components in from the palette, reorder elements, and move them into a different parent.

## Decided

- There is no text editor for humans. Direct editing means working on the drawn design, not on its data.
- The element is the primitive, and an element's position lives on its parent.

## Suggested (cursory, not prescriptive)

- Edits follow the same validation rules as proposals, so a human can't save a design that fails them.
- Agreed earlier: this comes after notes and building from a design, though the human expects the order to shift as the work goes.

## Open

- Whether a human's edit saves straight away or on a Save action, and whether each edit becomes a version. Saving a version per drag would make history hard to use.
- What happens if a human edits while the design agent has a proposal waiting.
- Which of the plan's details the human wants. The inspector panel and color picker came from the plan and haven't been discussed.

## Not in this feature

An editable theme with "promote to token", a project's own component library as the palette, and grid and stack containers.
title: design: direct editing
